snp1.7:1.5: A methodical almsround means not skipping any donors along the way—one of the thirteen ascetic (dhutaṅga) practices. See Thag 16:7.
snp1.7:5.1: Birds and reptiles are called “twice-born” because the laying of the egg counts as the first birth, and the hatching of the chick or baby reptile from the egg counts as the second.
snp1.7:18.3: This line is a pointed comment on what Aggika Bhāradvāja himself has just done to the Buddha.
snp1.7:23.3: The Vibhaṅga to the fourth pārājika rule explains that someone who falsely claims superior human attainments—the four jhānas and the noble attainments—is the greatest kind of thief in the world, since they are, in effect, stealing the almsfood offered by the countryside.
snp1.7:27.1: The Sutta Nipāta commentary explains the “divine chariot” as standing for the eight concentration attainments: the four jhānas and the four formless states.
